cards.text: It's the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, and the LORD speaks to His prophet Jeremiah. Take a scroll, He says, and write on it all the words I've spoken to you about Israel, Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you under Josiah until today. Friend, that's a WHOLE career, not a sticky note.

cards.question: God wants the people of Judah to hear about the calamity He plans to bring on them. What does He hope each of them will do?
Jeremiah has years of the LORD's words to get onto that scroll. Who does he call to write them down as he speaks?

cards.text: Baruch, a scribe, writes down every word as Jeremiah dictates, and then there's a snag: Jeremiah says he's restricted and can't enter the house of the LORD. Biggest project of your life, finally DONE, and your badge won't open the door.

cards.question: Jeremiah can't go into the house of the LORD himself, so he tells Baruch to go there and read the scroll aloud to the people.
Jeremiah hopes the people will turn from their wicked ways. He says that's because great is the LORD's ___ against this people.

cards.text: Baruch does everything Jeremiah commanded him. Then, in the ninth month of Jehoiakim's fifth year, a fast before the LORD is called for all the people of Jerusalem and everyone who's come in from the cities of Judah.
Baruch reads from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, up in the upper courtyard by the New Gate. Every person there hears it.

cards.question: Gemariah's son Micaiah hears all the words of the LORD from the scroll. Where does he go next?

answers.text: The scribe's chamber in the king's palace
The house of Jonathan the secretary

cards.text: All the officials are sitting there, including Elishama the scribe and Micaiah's own father, Gemariah. Micaiah tells them everything Baruch read. You walk into the big meeting with major news, and your DAD is sitting on the panel.

cards.question: The officials send a man named Jehudi to tell Baruch to stop reading the scroll in public.

cards.text: When Baruch arrives, the officials say, "Please sit down," and ask him to read it to them. So he does, and two readings in, this man is officially ON TOUR.

cards.question: The officials hear every word Baruch reads from the scroll. How do they react?

answers.text: They turn to one another in fear
They laugh and wave it all off
They walk out before Baruch finishes

cards.question: After hearing the scroll, the officials tell Baruch they must report all these words to the king.
The officials ask Baruch how he wrote all these words. Baruch tells them he copied them from an older scroll.
Before taking these words to the king, the officials tell Baruch that he and Jeremiah must ___ themselves and tell no one where they are.

cards.text: The officials store the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, then go to King Jehoiakim in the courtyard and report everything. I know that walk, friend. It's the walk I made across the Millers' counter every time I stamped a cookie crooked. Slow. Smiling. Mustache already up in surrender.

cards.question: King Jehoiakim hears the officials' report about the scroll and sends ___ to get it.

cards.text: It's the ninth month, so the king is sitting in his winter quarters with a fire burning in front of him. Jehudi reads to the king, and all the officials stand beside him. The king sits, everybody else stands. Friend, after years flat on my back in a drawer, standing sounds like a PROMOTION.

cards.question: Jehudi reads the scroll to King Jehoiakim. Every time Jehudi gets through three or four columns, what does the king do?

answers.text: Cuts them off and throws them in the fire
Hands them to an official to keep
Tells Jehudi to read them once more

cards.question: Jehoiakim cuts the columns with a scribe's ___ and keeps going until the entire scroll is ___ by the fire.
As King Jehoiakim and his servants hear all these words, they become frightened and tear their garments.
While the scroll burns, three officials named Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah are in the room. What do they do?

answers.text: Urge the king not to burn it
Help throw columns into the fire
Leave the room before it's done

cards.question: Jehoiakim won't listen to those three officials. Instead, he orders men to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet.
The king sends three men to seize Baruch and Jeremiah. But who had hidden them?

cards.text: After the king burns the scroll, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah. Jehoiakim had the fire. God still has the last word.

cards.question: The first scroll is burned up. What does the LORD tell Jeremiah to do now?

answers.text: Write the very same words on another scroll
Stop speaking to the king for good
Leave Jerusalem with Baruch at once

cards.text: The LORD also has a message for Jehoiakim, and He quotes the king's own question back to him: why did you write that the king of Babylon would surely come and destroy this land? When your own words get read back to you, friend, the meeting is NOT going your way.

cards.question: Because Jehoiakim burned the scroll, the LORD says he will have no one to sit on ___ throne.
The LORD says Jehoiakim's body will be buried with honor beside his fathers.
The LORD says He will punish Jehoiakim, his descendants and his servants. What does He say He is punishing them for?

cards.text: And it reaches past the palace. The LORD says He'll bring all the calamity He warned about on the people of Jerusalem and the men of Judah, because they did not listen.

cards.question: Jeremiah gives Baruch another scroll, and as Jeremiah dictates, Baruch writes all the words of the burned scroll again. Many similar words are added to them.
